question: A sector of a circle has a central angle of 90 degrees and a radius of 10 cm. Another sector of the same circle has a central angle of pi/4 radians. What is the ratio of the area of the first sector to the area of the second sector?
solution:
**Given:**

Sector 1 angle = 90°

Sector 2 angle = π/4 radians

Radius = 10 cm (same for both)

**Formula used:**

Area of sector (in degrees) = θ/360 × πr²

Area of sector (in radians) = 1/2 × r² × θ

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area₁ = 90/360 × π × 10²

⇒ Area₁ = 1/4 × 100π = 25π

⇒ Area₂ = 1/2 × 10² × π/4

⇒ Area₂ = 1/2 × 100 × π/4 = 50π/4 = 12.5π

⇒ Ratio = Area₁ ÷ Area₂

⇒ Ratio = 25π ÷ 12.5π = 2

**∴ Ratio = 2 : 1**
